generation.mode: built-in imagegen edit with the edit target first and the canon second as reference only

lighting_isotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient magnitude peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; final water-mask pixels and gradients below 12 luminance units excluded
lighting_isotropy.visual_check: No whole-cell cast-shadow field or time-of-day gradient is visible, but the generated basalt columns have brighter tops and darker faces and several conifers have lighter and darker sides. The aggregate metric does not establish the literal no-lit-side rule.

median_conifer_crown_final_scale.measurement: Manual median full-crown width across 20 representative isolated conifers distributed over the source, scaled by 2560/1254. A repeatable dark-green component detector found 102 candidates with a 17 source-pixel dark-core median, independently confirming that the crowns are materially underscale.

buildable_vs_steep_fraction.basis: manual estimated fraction of non-water land area
buildable_vs_steep_fraction.method: The broad coherent gold-green shelf, open central meadow, gentle southern draw, and adjoining open moor count as buildable; exposed east and south cliff faces count as steep; dense conifer groups, talus, scattered outcrops, and rough plateau make up the remainder.

water_mask.encoding: opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha
water_mask.derivation: Connected source-raster teal classification, bounded growth through adjacent cool wet pixels, short-gap raster closure through source-visible stone-occluded stream reaches, two-pixel edge inclusion for wash and spray, full enclosed-hole filling required by the cell contract, and forced inclusion of every east-edge pixel. No polyline supplies the mask boundary.
water_mask.component_note: Two dry-stone occlusions divide the upstream stream into two small source-visible wet components; the pool, fall, and coast form the third component. The complete mask is hole-free.

source_scale_gate_proxy.note: Local source-scale reproduction of the repository blue-fringe predicate at radii that scale to approximately 6 px and 49 px on the 2560 px canvas.

water_mask.manual_overlay_review: The diagnostic overlay shows the mask covering the painted sea, surf and stack wash, the full pool, waterfall sheet and spray, and every source-visible stream reach without swallowing dry meadow or dry cliff faces.

open_risks: The candidate is not promotable under the stated hard scale constraint: representative full crowns measure about 49.0 px / 2.352 m at the final canvas scale, below the required 84-147 px / 4-7 m range, and many individual crowns are visibly smaller.
The source paints sea across 93 pixels of the north edge at the north-east corner instead of ending that edge dry except for the corner pixel. The water mask truthfully follows the painted extent.

Several cliff sections are regular runs of similarly sized columns with bright top planes and darker vertical faces. This misses both the weathered-irregular basalt rule and the literal equal-value-on-every-side lighting rule even though aggregate directionality is low.
The conspicuous road, strip, ditch, and wall defect is absent, but the southern side of the shelf still contains scattered small conifers and rocks instead of remaining completely clear open meadow.
No second ImageGen call was made because the task authorizes a retry only for a non-square result; the returned source was square.
Seam continuity, terrain naturalism, exact water-mask judgment, and overall visual quality remain director and owner decisions; this report does not claim visual acceptance.
